blocks.text:
I'm working through the spatial coordinates to figure out which residues in chain A's range fall close enough to chain B's helix segment to count as contacts, trying to narrow it down region by region rather than checking every atom pair.

I'm checking whether chain A residues with positive z-coordinates around 12-19 but low x-values (like the 29-31 region) could be close enough to chain B's K341, but the x-coordinates don't quite line up—B's x is in the 12-16 range while these A residues sit near -2 to -5, so they're likely too far apart to be true contacts.

So I'm scanning more broadly through chain A for atoms with z roughly 8-16 and x roughly 0-12, listing out candidates like residues 26, 29-31, 52, 72, 120, 124, 149, 150, 151, and 152, then cross-referencing against chain B's 348-352 stretch (SER, GLU, PHE, GLN, LEU) to see which pairs actually fall within contact distance.

Continuing through residues 30-35, I'm tracking z-coordinates clustering around 10-21 with x-values spanning roughly -11 to 2.5, picking out which side chains like OG, CG, CB, OE1 sit in this high-z region of chain A.

Now I'm scanning for where chain A and chain B might actually meet spatially - checking residues 341-353 on chain B which have positive x extending up toward 16, then shifting to chain A's residues 148-149 (SER, TRP) where y goes negative and z drops to the 3-7 range, comparing backbone and side-chain atom positions to find a plausible interface.

Finishing the arginine coordinates, I'm now checking the distance between chain A ASP151's backbone oxygen and chain B R343's NH1 guanidinium nitrogen, computing the vector components to estimate a potential salt-bridge contact of roughly 4 angstroms.

Checking D151's OD1 against R343's NH1 instead, I find a much tighter distance of about 2.6 angstroms, confirming a real contact between these residues. This points to the interface region being around chain A 148-152 and chain B 341-348, so I'm now pulling alpha-carbon coordinates for chain B residues 341 through 351 to map out the full interface more systematically.

I continue listing chain B alpha-carbon positions through residue 361, confirming it's a helical stretch, then start scanning chain A for atoms with z-coordinates above 7 to find which residues could be spatially close to this helix—checking stretches around residues 21-36 and noting their z-values climb into the relevant range around residues 27-35.

Working through more chain A residues with x negative and z 8-21, I find candidates in the 3-17 range (including residues 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 14, 17, 33) plus residues 147-152 showing varied z-values. Cross-referencing with chain B's negative-x, high-z atoms narrows things down to residues 349, 352, 353, 355, 356, and 359 as likely contact points between the two chains.

Checking coordinates more closely, chain B's K359 appears to sit near chain A's residues around position 41-47, based on overlapping y-values in the -9 to -16 range alongside matching x-coordinates in the -8 to -13 window — this looks like a promising interface region to examine further.

I'm continuing to scan nearby chain A residues like PHE, GLY, VAL, and ILE for their coordinates, checking whether any fall close enough to chain B's A357 residue to count as a contact.

Looking further, I note chain B's R358 coordinates but find no chain A atoms nearby, suggesting residues 358-361 may lack any interface contacts. I decide to take a more systematic approach, mapping out which chain A atoms fall within the spatial region where chain B's residues are located so I can compute minimum distances more reliably.

Continuing to list chain A CA coordinates through residues 25-36, tracking their positions for proximity comparison with chain B.

Still computing the coordinate sequence...

Still listing coordinate points...

Still generating coordinate points...

Still listing coordinate points...

Now I'm checking distances between chain A CA coordinates and chain B residues to find contacts within roughly 12 Å, computing pairwise distances to identify which chain A residues sit near the chain B region around residues 341-345.

That pair is too far apart, so I rule out contact there and shift to checking the region near chain A residues 148-152 instead. I'm scanning chain B residues 346-348 against nearby chain A atoms, finding residue 30's glutamate side chain coordinates fall in a similar x/z range, so I check its positioning next.

The key finding is a 3.3 Å contact between Chain B His346's NE2 and Chain A Glu30's OE2 atoms, confirming a genuine interface contact there, while the CE1-OE2 and ND1-OE2 distances are too long to count. This suggests the interface around chain A residues 28-37 pairs with chain B residues 341-353, so I move on to checking Chain B Lys345's coordinates against nearby chain A atoms in that x/y/z range.

I find another contact: B:Lys345's NZ atom sits 3.85 Å from A:Glu30's OE2, confirming that lysine also bridges the interface, though its OE1 distance is too far. Checking the neighboring K341 and Tyr342 residues, I don't find any chain A atoms close enough to K341 to count as contacts, so I move on to checking Tyr342's position against the interface.

Working through Tyr342's ring atoms, I find its hydroxyl oxygen comes within 3.35 Å of Ser29's OG on chain A, establishing another genuine contact pair. I'm now checking whether the tyrosine ring also approaches Gln35, measuring distances from its CZ and CE2 carbons toward the glutamine's side-chain oxygen and nitrogen.

I confirm Y342's CE2 sits 3.94 Å from Gln35's NE2, so that's a second contact. This suggests the interface spans chain A residues around 29-37 contacting chain B near 342-353, plus a possible second patch near chain A 148-152, and maybe a third involving residues 38-58/69-73 against chain B 350-357 — so I'm pulling the coordinates for Phe350's backbone and side-chain atoms to test that region next.

Checking Phe350's side chain against Asn37, I find contacts: OD1 comes within 4.1 Å of CE2 and within 3.77 Å of CZ, confirming A:Asn37 touches B:Phe350. Given how error-prone this is manually, I need to systematically scan every chain B residue against nearby chain A atoms, so I'm narrowing down the coordinate ranges for chain A atoms worth checking in detail.

I'm grouping chain B's CA positions into three spatial clusters to speed up filtering, then going through chain A residues checking distances from their CA atoms to each cluster's center. I'm flagging several chain A residues (around positions 28-35, 73, 150-152) that fall within roughly 14 Å of the first cluster's center, since these are the ones likely to contain atoms within actual contact range.

Now I'm compiling the exact atomic coordinates for chain B residues 341-343 (Lys, Tyr, Arg) so I can do precise per-atom distance calculations against the flagged chain A residues rather than relying on CA-only approximations.

Still listing residue coordinates...

Still listing residue coordinates...

Still parsing atomic coordinates...

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Now I'm checking which chain A atoms fall inside the bounding box for residue B341, filtering by x, y, and z ranges, and finding that none of the candidate atoms satisfy all constraints, so B341 likely has no contact within 4 angstroms.

Moving to B342, I'm defining a tighter bounding box and scanning chain A residues near it (29,30,34-37,55-56,69-70,73,152), checking each atom's coordinates against the x/y/z bounds to see if any fall within 4 angstroms of the OH atom, so far finding S29's backbone atoms excluded due to distance.

For S29, CB and OG fall within the box, and I'm computing the actual distance from CB to OH, getting roughly 3.61 angstroms, confirming a contact. For E30, all atoms except the backbone either fall outside the z-range or the distance to the nearest B342 atom exceeds 4 angstroms, ruling out contact. Now I'm checking GLN35's CB and CG atoms, computing distances to the OH and CZ atoms to see if they fall within the contact threshold.

For GLN35's CD atom, I find a distance of 3.78 to OH, confirming a contact, and NE2 shows a contact distance of 3.94 to CE2, confirming Q35. I'm now walking through TRP36's full atom coordinates and checking distances from its O atom to OH and CZ, finding both exceed 4 angstroms with no contact. Moving to ASN37, I'm listing its N, CA, C, O, and CB coordinates to begin the same distance check against B342.

Continuing ASN37's CG, OD1, and ND2 coordinates, I compare OD1 against B342's CZ and OH, finding distances of 3.28 and 2.57 respectively — both confirming contacts. I check SER152 and rule it out due to its y-coordinate being far outside range. Then checking LEU73's CD1 against B342's CD1, I calculate a distance of 3.47, confirming another contact between A:L73 and B:Y342, so I'm now going back to verify LEU73's full atom coordinates to be sure.

I also check LEU73's CD2 against B342's atoms and find both distances too large to count. Checking LEU73 against B343's CG and CD atoms, the CG distance comes out to about 4.02 — just over the 4.0 cutoff so no contact — but testing CB against CG gives 3.97, which confirms LEU73 also contacts B343.

So now I'm compiling my list of chain B residues contacting chain A: Y342, R343, K345, H346, F350 so far. I'm scanning B343 ARG's bounding box against chain A atoms, going residue by residue — starting with THR52 (out of range) and PHE53, whose CA, CB, and ring atoms all sit at low z-values near 3.6, while B343's minimum z is around 6, so I'm checking whether any pairs still fall under the 4Å cutoff.

I'm checking LYS54's CD, CE, and CB atoms against B343's CD and CG, finding distances just above 4Å, so K54 likely doesn't qualify as a contact. Then I move to ARG71, which is excluded since its CA sits outside the y-range, and now I'm pulling in PHE72's backbone and side-chain coordinates to continue the distance check.

Q147 is too far out on the y-axis, so that's a no. But D151's OD1 comes in at 2.62Å from B343's NH1 - that's a solid contact, confirming R343 interacts with D151. Now checking S152's coordinates to see if it's close enough to matter too.

Working through the distances, S152's CB sits about 3.78Å from B343's backbone oxygen - close enough to count as a contact, so R343 touches S152 as well. The CA-to-backbone distances don't pan out though. So overall R343 engages L73, D151, and S152, confirming it belongs in the contact list.

Now I'm shifting to K344, defining its bounding box and checking which chain A atoms fall within it - S152's atoms are in range, so I'm pulling up K344's backbone coordinates to start measuring actual distances.

Checking each pairing between S152's atoms and K344's backbone, the distances all come out around 4.5Å or more - none close enough to count as contact. I also rule out N150 and L73 since their coordinates fall outside K344's z-range or are too far on the z-axis. So K344 doesn't make the contact list.

Now I'm setting up the bounding box for K345 and starting to check chain A atoms that might fall within it, beginning with E30's side chain positions.

Working through the distances between E30's glutamate side chain and K345's lysine atoms, I find OE2 to NZ comes out to 3.85Å - close enough to confirm a real contact. K345 makes the list through this E30 interaction, and H346 is already confirmed via its earlier NE2-OE2 contact with E30.

Now I'm setting up the bounding box for K347 and identifying which chain A atoms could fall within its range - mainly looking at S152's side chain since it has the right z-coordinates, then listing out all of K347's atomic coordinates to prepare for distance calculations.

Checking S152's O, C against K347's CD and CE puts the closest distance at roughly 4.2Å, which falls just short of contact range. Testing other nearby chain A atoms like residue 150's ND2 and OD1 against K347's NZ also comes up empty, with distances well above 4Å. After double-checking the precise coordinates for S152's O and K347's CD, the distance confirms at 4.21Å - still no contact, so K347 gets excluded from the list, and I'm moving on to set up the bounding box for S348.

Scanning chain A for atoms matching S348's spatial constraints (negative y, z above 13) turns up nothing - most chain A atoms in this z-range cluster around positive y values near residues 28-33. S348 gets excluded too, so now I'm setting up the bounding box for E349 and pulling its atom coordinates to compare against nearby chain A residues like 29, 30, 32, and 34-37.

Checking A29's hydroxyl group against E349's OE1 gives a distance under 4Å - that's a contact. F350 already confirmed with N37. Now I'm narrowing down Q351's bounding box and checking whether any chain A atoms near residues 150-152 fall within its y and z ranges, finding most fall just outside the x boundary.

Testing the CB atom of A152 against Q351's OE1 shows too large a gap, and checking A149's backbone carbonyl against Q351's NE2 also comes up too far away, so I'm ruling out any Q351 contact entirely.

Moving to L352, I'm defining its bounding box and scanning chain A for residues in the matching y, x, and z ranges, finding most candidates like residues 16-22 and 38-41 fall outside the needed z or x range, so I continue checking residues 106-113 next.

I keep scanning chain A systematically by residue number, checking each atom's coordinates against L352's bounding box, and so far every candidate residue from 3 through 26 is too far in x or y from L352's actual position.

I'm now checking whether chain B's 357-361 region (lower z values) could pair with chain A's 20-23 residues, since those sit in a plausible negative x/y range that might overlap.

Computing the distance between A's Gly23 CA and B's Ala357 backbone oxygen gives roughly 3.3 Å — that's a genuine contact, so I need to revise my assumption and treat A357 as contacting G23. This means I have to re-scan chain A residues 20-24 and nearby loops against B354-361 more carefully, since the helix seems to cross directly over this region.

I'm checking residues D19 through P21 against the B359/B361 side chain atoms one by one, computing coordinate differences to rule out or confirm proximity, and so far none of these residues fall close enough to count as contacts.

Now I'm testing V22's side chain atoms against B359 and B360 — comparing CG1 against their backbone and carbonyl oxygens — and finding one pair (V22 CG1 vs B359 O) close enough at roughly 4.2 Å that I want to verify more precisely.

For G23, the oxygen of B357 is within contact range at 3.33 Å, so that's a confirmed hit, though B358's nitrogen is still too far.

I'm now checking V24's atoms against B357's beta carbon and nitrogen, computing several distances in the 4.0-4.1 Å range that are borderline — close to the cutoff but likely just outside it, and continuing to check V24's oxygen against the same residue.

Now I'm confirming B357 as ALA contacts chain A, then moving to scan B354 through B361 systematically. For B354 VAL, I'm comparing its atoms against nearby chain A residues like A39 VAL, and finding that A39's CG2 and B354's CG2 land right around 3.97 Å apart — a solid contact worth logging.

Next I'm checking B355 ASP against nearby chain A atoms, scanning residues like A41 PHE in the relevant coordinate range to see if their side chains fall within contact distance.

Then I'm working through B356 GLN, measuring distances to chain A residues around positions 20, 23, and 25 to find any that might be close enough to count as contacts.

Comparing B356's CB atom to A25's CB atom gives a distance of about 3.92, which qualifies as a contact, so I'm adding Q356 to the list.

Now I'm shifting to B358 ARG, scanning through chain A residues near G23, V22, and the A41-A44 range to check which atoms fall within contact distance.

I find that A41's CZ atom and B358's CB atom are about 3.78 apart, confirming a contact, so R358 contacts F41 on chain A.

Next I'm moving to B359 LYS, checking its coordinate range against nearby chain A residues like V22, P20/21, and G23 to see which ones might be close enough to count as contacts.

Checking distances from K359's O and C and CB atoms to V22's various side chain atoms, the closest I get is around 4.2-5.4 Å, which is too far. Testing against G23's N atom and other chain A positions near residue 22-23 also comes up short at roughly 4.5 Å minimum. So it looks like K359 has no qualifying contact with chain A.

Moving to B360 (glycine), I check its backbone atoms against V22's gamma carbons across several distance calculations, getting values like 4.39, 4.82, and 4.08 Å — all just over the 4.0 threshold, so still no contact there either. I'm now checking A22's CB atom against B360's atoms to see if that pairing works.

Next I move to B361 (tyrosine), scanning chain A residues 41-44 (phenylalanine through glutamate) for atoms falling within the relevant coordinate ranges to test as potential contact partners.

Checking A41 CZ against CD2 gives about 5.3, too far. But A41 CD2 to B361 CE2 comes out to roughly 3.99, which looks like a genuine contact — I want to double-check this one precisely with the exact coordinates.

Computing it exactly: dx=-0.341, dy=-3.198, dz=-2.371, giving a distance of about 3.996 — just barely under the 4.0 cutoff, so this is a real but marginal contact. I'll also scan other A41-B361 distances for comparison, which come out to 4.13 and 4.47, both too far. Then checking A42 backbone atoms against B361, I find O to OH gives a distance around 2.60, which is a solid contact.

Confirming this: A42 O to B361 OH works out to roughly 2.61 Å, a clear hit, so Tyr361 is confirmed as contacting Gly42. Checking nearby A43 atoms shows no contact, but A42 C to OH gives about 3.82, another valid contact — so Y361 definitely belongs in my contact list.

Now I'm going back to double-check earlier residues I might have missed, starting with B349-B353. For B352 (Leu), I'm comparing its coordinate ranges against chain A atoms to rule out proximity, since the earlier analysis suggested only residues 150-152 and residue 17's region overlap in that z/y range — checking Gln17 NE2 against B352 O shows they're too far apart (dx of 8.5). I'm continuing to check residue 16 (Leu) atoms next for any overlap.

Checking B351 against nearby chain A residues confirms no contact given the large z-distance from A152. Moving on, B349, B350, and B354 are confirmed contacts, with B354 pairing closely to A39's CG2 at about 3.97 Å, so I'm checking neighboring atoms like A38 and A39's other side chains to make sure there isn't an even closer distance before finalizing.

Recomputing the A39-B354 distance precisely gives 3.97 Å, confirming this is a valid contact just under the 4 Å threshold. Now I'm examining B355's atoms to find which chain A residues sit near its position around y=-10, z=9-12.

B355 doesn't appear to make any contact with chain A. For B356, the CB-to-A25-CB distance checks out at 3.92 Å, and the OG/CG side-chain distances to A25 also fall within range, confirming that contact. B357's backbone and side-chain atoms line up near A24's amide nitrogen and A25's hydroxyl, giving a confirmed contact around 4.03 Å and 3.9 Å respectively.

I've already verified 346, 347, 345, 342, and 343, so I'm moving to check B346's other possible contacts beyond E30 — testing distances to A29 and A35 side chains, which both come back too far (5.3 Å and more). So B346's only real contact remains the NE2-OE2 interaction with E30 at 3.30 Å, and I'm pulling up E30's exact OE2 coordinates to double-check that measurement.

Checking H346's NE2 against E30's OE2 confirms a 3.30 Å contact, while the CE1 to OE2 distance comes out to 4.14 Å, too far to count. B345's NZ-to-OE2 distance checks out at 3.85 Å, but its CE atom to A30's OE2 is over 4 Å. I'm now running through chain B residues 341 through 361 confirming which ones have contacts: 342, 343, 345, 346, 349, 350, 353, 354, 356, 357, 358, and 361 are in, while 341, 344, 347, 348, 351, 352, 355, 359, and 360 are out. I want to double-check several of the "no contact" residues more carefully, and verify my assumption that chain A atoms with z greater than 8 and negative y are confined to residues 150-152 and 16-17 by scanning through the full atom list again.

I'm going residue by residue through chain A (3 through 27 so far), tracking the y and z coordinate ranges for each, and cross-referencing specific atoms like LYS14's NZ and the side chains of residues 17, 21, and 24 against chain B's x-coordinate range to rule out any additional nearby contacts.

For residue 27, I check its backbone atoms against B353's side chain atoms and find that A27's nitrogen is within 4 angstroms of B353's CD2 carbon — a genuine contact, though B353 is already captured in my contact list. I continue scanning forward into residues 28 and 29.

I keep working through the y/z coordinate ranges for residues 29 through 52, flagging anything near chain B. For residue 52, a threonine, I check its oxygen and carbon atoms against the nearby B354 side chain atoms but find all distances exceed the 4 angstrom cutoff, so no contact there.

Now checking residue 54, a lysine, against B350's atoms—the CZ and CD1 positions. The CD distance comes out just over 4, but the CG and CB atoms to CD1 fall within range at roughly 3.6-3.9 angstroms, confirming contact. Then for residue 55, a leucine, the nitrogen is about 4.2 angstroms from B350's CE1 due to the z-difference, so no contact there either.

Moving through residues 56-75, I'm screening by y and z ranges to rule out contacts with B341/342 (different x range entirely) and checking chain A's higher-numbered residues against B344 and B347. For B344, the closest candidate is A152's backbone oxygen, but the y-distance of about 5.6 angstroms rules it out. For B347, I'm now checking whether A152's carbon and oxygen atoms, which sit at similar z-heights, come close enough.

I'm computing the distance from A152's oxygen to B347's delta carbon, getting roughly 4.21 angstroms, while the gamma carbon comes in too far at that x-offset, so B347 stays excluded with that 4.21 minimum. I move on to rule out B341, B348, B351, B352, and B355 as too distant, but B359 and B360 are borderline around 4.08-4.21 angstroms, so I want to re-verify those coordinates carefully. Checking V22's gamma carbon against B360's backbone nitrogen and alpha carbon, the distances come out around 5.6 angstroms, so I'm now scanning chain A for residues with y below -13 to find anything closer, landing on glutamate 44 and its side chain atoms as a candidate to check next.

Scanning through chain A residues 44 through 50 and 135-142, I find nothing close enough to B360's coordinates—the nearest candidate from glutamate 44's gamma carbon is still about 4.3 angstroms away in x, confirming B360's true nearest contact is the 4.08 value from V22, so it stays excluded, and similarly B359 stays excluded at 4.21. I then move to double-check B358's contact with phenylalanine 41's zeta carbon, computing the component distances between that atom and B358's beta carbon to verify the 3.78 angstrom figure.

I confirm the Y361 contact through A42's oxygen at 2.61 angstroms, then verify B349's contact distance using A29's gamma oxygen against B349's glutamate OE1—working through the x, y, z differences to arrive at roughly 3.49 angstroms, which checks out. I verify B350 contacts through A54's gamma carbon at 3.59 and N37's zeta carbon at 3.77, then move to recheck B345 using E30's OE2 and K345's NZ coordinates, computing the distance components to confirm approximately 3.85 angstroms. I then rule out B341 against A30/A31 due to large x-coordinate separation, and start checking B342 against A33/A34's methionine atoms.

Compiling the full list of chain B contact residues now: Y342, R343, K345, H346, E349, F350, L353, V354, Q356, A357, R358, and Y361. I go back to verify there's nothing missed for B344 and B348, then test K347's NZ against A150's ND2 region—finding a 5.46 angstrom z-difference, too far to count. I check B351's NE2 against A149's backbone oxygen and rule that out too, then test B354's CG1 against A41's zeta and epsilon carbons, both yielding distances too large for contact. I'm now starting to check B353's CD1 coordinate against nearby atoms.

Checking K347, K359, and G360 distances confirms they're borderline but fine to exclude. I verify B348's SER sidechain against A29/A30 and find it too far, so it's excluded, then move to check B352 against A17/A27 for proximity.

Those also turn out too distant to count. I run through a few more pairs (B355 vs A27, B344 vs A73/A74) and none meet the distance threshold, so I'm done with the contact analysis.
